title: The Darensbourg family and Willie Foster
summary: Russell asks about Joe Darensbourg and Willie Foster; Roubleau says Caffrey's family came from his hometown, his father played mandolin and guitar, and Caffrey died in Texas.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yeah. I knew Joe Darnsberg out in California that plays with Tedore Clarinetist. Do you remember? Was he any member of that family?
Joe Darnsberg? I know. I can't recall him. I know. I know.
And then I was up in Baton Rouge about two years ago. And we interviewed Willie Foster, one of the old-time guitar players. He played guitar, I think, more than he did banjo.
Willie Foster?
Yes. The brother of Pops Foster, George Foster, the bass player.

Willie Foster. Willie Foster. His first instrument that I could recall, or I would, was a violin. That's right. He said he played violin. From a violin, then he started playing guitar in the banjo with a foster.
Well, he's the only one we saw up in Baton Rouge, but they told us there were some Darnsberg men up there, musicians by the name of Darnsberg.
Do you know any of those?
Well, that's the Darnsberg they're talking about.

The Cafferys family? That's the Darnsberg he's talking about. See, that's the Darnsberg he's talking about. He was up there, too. Because his father, Cafferys' father, used to play a mandolin and guitar. Yeah. His father. And they were from up around there, then? Right in my hometown.
Mm-hmm. Went up to Baton Rouge.
Right there, in Colonies, on the other side of the road, about 45 miles.
Yeah. Same family and all that. That's it.
And Cafferys' uncle, he was a trombone player.
Trombone.
Cafferys' uncle.
Are any of those men still living?
No.
No. Probably none of them. None of them still living. Like, if they were, I thought we'd try to find them someday.
No.
Maybe go up there and try to see them.
No, they're not living, Caffer not living himself.
No, I thought I heard, I think he died in Texas.
In Texas.
